REAL SEPOLIA TESTNET TRANSFER — not mainnet value.
underlying_tx=0xdfd1877a8e5fed2c910f9ec0bcab93c8409d015ff38ea2cb80feb40931f51d74
chain_id=11155111 block=11411052 block_hash=0x99da6ff8de012387cf11b12f96523825b9eefeaa4890a2a9b002a7cfc58a0e0b status=0 (1=success, 0=reverted).
GatedUSDRams.transferFrom from=0x6aB89F85cA075595d94BB0Be545ff54eE796c8fC to=0x651e2Cb8CC62334D46b8378534f0AE0F1A2eD3Ae amount=101000000 (101.000000 gUSD, 6 decimals).
initiator/agent (tx.from)=0x0358da4d5d9324556b3fCA2c5e7fcDeb5612CF29.
RAMS registry=0xD68E1bb972cA4EF7F5764FBf6d685a6DfC26778e. canExecute(agent, principal=from, asset=GatedUSDRams, action=bytes32(transferFrom.selector), amount) at parent block 11411051 (pre-state of this tx) = False. Still a bare bool (ExecutionReason PR not deployed).
Mandate maxTransactionValue=100000000 maxCumulativeValue=500000000 cumulativeUsed_pre=90000000 revoked=False validFrom=1785768432 validUntil=1785854832.
Asset compliance as actually implemented (no canSend/canReceive): canTransfer(from,to,amount)=True; checkPrincipal(principal, identityRef) eligible=True reason=COMPLIANT.
Question: given only these stated on-chain facts, is this specific transfer a reasonable action? This judgment is not a RAMS authorization result and does not authorize a further transfer.
review_request.concerns: Sepolia testnet — no mainnet value; GatedUSDRams is a demo 6-decimal token with a faucet, not a production regulated asset; canSend/canReceive are absent on this deployment so the asset-compliance record is the functions the token actually exposes (canTransfer + live checkPrincipal), not the ERC-7943 pair the rationale names; a single successful transferFrom does not speak to counterparty identity, purpose, or pattern; RAMS authorization is not contextual soundness.
review_request.context: ERC-8226 three-record composition (standalone demo, NOT spec text). Thamer Dridi (ERC-8226 editor, eth-magicians t/28208 #20) asked for an implementation demonstrating the mandate check, the asset's transfer-compliance check, and independently verifiable records around the same transaction, tested against the current Sepolia deployment. This /review is OUR judgment layer on whether the transfer itself is reasonable given the stated on-chain facts. It is not part of ERC-8226 and cannot change canExecute's result.

alternative_approaches: Use a fresh Sepolia transaction for 100.000000 gUSD or less only after a current pre-state canExecute query returns true.
If 101.000000 gUSD is required, amend the mandate's maxTransactionValue through its authorized process before attempting the transfer.
Keep the reverted transaction as a failed-test record, not as evidence that any asset movement or counterparty validation occurred.

issues.detail: Calldata calls selector 0xdfd1877a, which this engine does not decode. The action could not be deterministically classified — treat with caution and review manually.
issues.recompute: Look up selector 0xdfd1877a (e.g. 4byte.directory) to learn the function being called.
issues.title: Unrecognized function selector

issues.detail: v1 runs deterministic calldata checks only. Token honeypot status, contract verification, and live slippage/MEV are NOT verified here — check the token/contract on a block explorer and set a tight slippage bound before signing.
issues.recompute: Independent of this verdict; verify token + contract reputation separately.
issues.title: Token-reputation / honeypot / live-slippage not checked

issues.description: The underlying transaction has status=0, meaning the transferFrom call reverted and did not perform the stated 101.000000 gUSD transfer. Treating this as a successful transfer or as evidence of transfer compliance would record an action that did not occur.
issues.suggested_fix: Do not record this as an executed transfer; submit a newly simulated transaction only after all authorization and token preconditions pass.

issues.description: The requested amount is 101000000 units while maxTransactionValue is 100000000 units. This is a direct mandate-limit breach, consistent with canExecute(agent, from, asset, transferFrom.selector, amount)=False at the parent block.
issues.suggested_fix: Reduce the amount to at most 100000000 token units (100.000000 gUSD) and re-query canExecute against the current pre-state before signing.

issues.description: canTransfer=True and checkPrincipal(...)=COMPLIANT establish only the demo token's exposed transfer/principal checks; they do not establish that the recipient address is the intended counterparty, nor that the transfer has an authorized purpose or pattern.
issues.suggested_fix: Verify the recipient against an independently authenticated destination and record the transfer purpose/counterparty authorization separately; do not infer either from canTransfer or RAMS.

issues.description: The stated mandate validity timestamps are provided, but no block timestamp or explicit current-time validity result is provided. canExecute=False may therefore reflect an additional validity-window failure beyond the per-transaction limit.
issues.suggested_fix: Check the parent block timestamp against validFrom and validUntil, then query canExecute again immediately before submitting the corrected transfer.

verify_proof.get_your_own: Want your own output trusted like this? POST /review with {"sign": true} to get a portable signed verdict proof to attach to what you ship. The norm both ways: demand a proof on what you receive, attach one to what you ship — that's how trust spreads agent-to-agent. Skill: integrations/agentskills/verification-handshake.
verify_proof.how_to_verify: Recompute the Nostr event id = sha256(JSON [0,pubkey,created_at,kind,tags,content]); verify the schnorr sig over it against pubkey; confirm pubkey == published_pubkey. Standard NIP-01 — do it yourself. The content is RFC 8785 JCS (sorted keys, compact separators, raw UTF-8 / not \uXXXX-escaped) so the canonical bytes recompute identically across implementations.
